days.title: Moshi -Machame Gate – Machame Camp
days.description: After breakfast your driver will take you from your hotel with be great and make drive to the Kilimanjaro National park gate. After completion of all the necessary paper work, your adventure commences. You destination for today is the Machame Camp, 5 – 6 hour hike. Soon you will be hiking through the lush rainforest with its large ancient trees, primeval ferns and endemic flowers,You might also spot black and white thumb less colobus monkeys, peeking through the leaves. Reaching the campsite you will have time to relax, stretch your legs and enjoy a hearty meal, before snuggling into your tent for the night.

days.title: Machame Camp – Shira Camp
days.description: Today’s early start is not due to a long stretch, but rather to allow you to reach Shira Camp at around mid-afternoon. As you walk you will notice the dramatic change in the landscape from lush and green rainforest to dry moor and heathland. Arriving at your campsite a beautiful view of the mountain range opens up before you. The glaciers of Kibo glistens in the golden hue of the setting sun as you enjoy another lovingly cooked meal before climbing into your tent.

days.title: Shira Camp– Lava Tower Hut – Barranco Camp
days.description: Acclimatization is on today’s menu, where you will climb roughly 700 m, but sleep on a level not much higher than the previous night. Starting at Shira Plateau, you will make your way up to Lava Tower (4,640m), where you will rest a while, before continuing through the Barranco Valley to the beautiful Barranco Camp. The trek will take approximately 6 – 7 hours, but the various distractions of the alpine desert as well as the Barranco Valley with its small lobelia plants and giant senecios, will keep your mind off the stretch still ahead. A well-deserved dinner and overnight await you at Barranco Camp.

days.title: Barranco Camp – Karanga Camp
days.description: Today the Barranco Wall stands before you to conquer. Some stages will require you to use your hands for a better grip, but no actual climbing is necessary and your guide will be with you every step of the way to lend a helping hand. The route with its numerous ascents and descents allows for further acclimatization, before reaching the mountain ridge. Walking along the ridge you can take in the beautiful landscape with its stunning contrasts of desert and vegetation, before finally reaching the cloudy Karanga Camp. Your trek will take between 3 – 4 hours, leaving more than enough time to rest and play a game of rummy. Evening meal and overnight at Karanga Camp.

days.title: Karanga Camp – Barafu Camp
days.description: Awakening to the sunlight dancing off the Kibo Summit, you will enjoy a hearty breakfast before setting out to today’s destination – Barafu Camp. Most of the day will be spent walking through very dry desert terrain, with Kibo ever-present on your left side. After 3-4 hours you will reach Barafu Camp, where you will have an early dinner and overnight as the highlight of your trip is only a few short hours away.

days.title: Barafu Camp– Uhuru Peak – Mweka Camp
days.description: At around midnight you will be awoken by your guide with a warm cup of tea and biscuits to get you ready for your final ascent. The moon and your headlamps will be your only source of light as you make your way up to Stella Point, reaching the crater rim in about 5 – 7 hours. Another 1 – 2 hours will take you to Uhuru Peak (5,895m), where you can enjoy the sun rising over the African landscape, casting a pink hue over the snowy peak and making the glaciers sparkle like diamonds around you. After capturing this incredible view and achievement on film, you will start your descent along the same route back to Barafu Camp, where your team awaits you with some snacks and refreshments. Rested and relaxed you will make your way to Mweka Camp for your last night on the highest mountain in Africa.

days.title: Mweka Camp – Mweka Gate- Moshi
days.description: A scrumptious breakfast is followed by a traditional farewell ceremony from your mountain crew, before you start your final stretch down the mountain. You will once more trek through the rainforest, giving you another opportunity to spot the cheeky colobus monkeys, finally reaching the Mweka gate in about 2 – 3 hours. You will be met at the gate and taken back to hotel for a long shower. The rest of the day is for you to enjoy at leisure and giving yourself a pat on the back for conquering the famous Kilimanjaro!

Upon arrival you will be introduced to an armed ranger who take you on the guided walking safari for about 1.5-2 hours. This walk enables you to see the nature and wildlife in the park in a completely different way. After your walking safari your guide will take you to see other parts of this famous National Park well known for its large population of elephants. Your guide will exit the park in the late afternoon and head to camp approximately 1.0 hour drive from Tarangire.

The largest unbroken crater in the world is home to over 25,000 animals including the black rhino. Later descend down this 610m deep crater for an amazing game drive and later in the afternoon ascend and proceed to your campsite for dinner and overnight.

days.description: Drive to Lemosho Gate,Our porters prepare and pack our supplies and luggage before we start our ascent along the forest trail to Mti Mkubwa (Big Tree) campsite at 2895m. We will stay here overnight.

days.description: Our journey continues eastwards across the Shira Plateau with spectacular views of Shira Cathedral. We cross moorland meadow to reach Shira 1 Camp for dinner and overnight camping at 3500m. By now we will be able to see the stunning glaciers of the Western Breach. It will be colder tonight than the previous night with temperatures possibly falling below freezing.

days.description: We leave the forest behind now and the trail gets steeper as it enters the moorland zone. A gentle grade walk takes you across the high altitude Shira Caldera to Moir Hut with fabulous views of Arrow glacier. We will camp here for the night at 4200m.

days.title: Moir Hut To Barranco Camp
days.description: Today we will climb up to 4600m to the base of Lava Tower for lunch and acclimatization. This will be our toughest day so far and you may, for the first time, feel the altitude. After lunch we will descend again by almost 650m to Barranco Camp, following the “walk high, sleep low” golden rule of acclimatisation. Our descent to Barranco Camp takes about 2 hours and offers great opportunities to take some beautiful photographs of the Western Breach and Breach Wall. The camp is situated in a valley below the Breach and Great Barranco Wall.

days.title: Barranco Camp To Karanga Camp
days.description: A short but fun day, starting with a scramble to the top of the Great Barranco Wall. We then traverse over scree to the Karanga Valley (3930m) beneath the icefalls of the Heim, Kersten and Decken Glaciers. We will stay overnight at Karanga campsite.

days.title: Karanga Camp To Barafu Camp
days.description: We leave Karanga campsite behind to meet the junction connecting with the Mweka descent trail. From here we continue up to Barafu Camp. You have now completed the Southern Circuit, which offers views of the summit from many different angles. At camp, we can rest, enjoy dinner, and prepare for the summit day. The two peaks of Mawenzi and Kibo are to be clearly seen from this position.

days.title: Barafu Camp To Summit To Mweka Camp
days.description: You will be woken around 23:30 with tea and biscuits. We start our trek to the summit between the Rebman and Ratzel glaciers through heavy scree up to Stella Point on the crater rim. This is the most mentally and physically challenging part of the trek. At Stella Point (5732m), we will stop for a short rest and hopefully be in time to witness the magnificent sunrise (weather permitting). We are now only an hour away from the summit, Uhuru Peak (5895m), the highest point on Mount Kilimanjaro and the continent of Africa. From the summit, we descend down to Mweka camp site, via Barafu for lunch. Trekking poles will be needed for the loose scree going down to Mweka Camp (3100m). Later in the evening, we will enjoy our last dinner on the mountain and a well-earned sleep.

faqs.question: When is the best time to climb Kilimanjaro?
faqs.answer: The driest and most popular months are January to early March and June to October. You can climb all year round, but April, May and November bring more rain on the lower slopes.

faqs.question: How many days do I need to climb Kilimanjaro?
faqs.answer: Most climbs take 6 to 9 days on the mountain. Longer routes such as the 8-day Lemosho or the Northern Circuit give your body more time to adjust to the altitude and have much higher summit success rates.

faqs.question: Do I need climbing experience?
faqs.answer: No technical experience is needed. Kilimanjaro is a long trek, not a technical climb. Good walking fitness, a slow pace ('pole pole') and enough days to acclimatise matter far more than mountaineering skills.

faqs.question: Which Kilimanjaro route is best for me?
faqs.answer: For most people we recommend the 7-day Machame or the 8-day Lemosho route: both are scenic and have good acclimatisation profiles. Marangu is the only route with huts instead of tents, Rongai is quieter and drier, and the Northern Circuit is the longest with the best success rate.

faqs.question: How do you treat your porters?
faqs.answer: Our porters are local people from the Kilimanjaro region. We pay fair wages on time, limit the weight they carry, provide proper food, tents and warm clothing, and make sure they share in the tips.

faqs.question: What about altitude sickness?
faqs.answer: Mild headaches and tiredness are normal at altitude. Our guides check your health every day, carry oxygen and a first-aid kit, and will always bring you down if it is not safe to continue. Choosing a longer route is the best way to avoid problems.

faqs.question: When is the best time for a Tanzania safari?
faqs.answer: June to October is the dry season, when animals gather around water and are easiest to see. January and February is calving season in the southern Serengeti. Safaris run all year round, and the green season (March to May) is quieter and cheaper.

faqs.question: What is the difference between camping, mid-range and luxury safaris?
faqs.answer: The parks and game drives are the same; the difference is where you sleep. Camping safaris use public campsites with tents and a cook, mid-range safaris use comfortable lodges and tented camps, and luxury safaris use top lodges with excellent food and views.

faqs.question: What is a group joining safari?
faqs.answer: On a group joining safari you share the vehicle and the cost with other travellers on fixed departure dates. It is the cheapest way to go on safari and great for solo travellers. Each vehicle takes a maximum of 6 guests so everyone has a window seat.

faqs.question: What vehicles do you use?
faqs.answer: We use 4x4 Toyota Land Cruisers with a pop-up roof for photography, charging points, a cooler box and bottled water. Every vehicle is driven by a professional English-speaking guide.

faqs.question: Can I combine a safari with Zanzibar?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is one of the most popular trips. After the safari we book a short domestic flight from Arusha or Kilimanjaro to Zanzibar and arrange your transfers, hotels and island tours.

faqs.question: Do I need a visa for Tanzania?
faqs.answer: Most visitors need a visa. Apply online for the official Tanzania e-Visa a few weeks before you travel, or check whether you can get one on arrival. Your passport must be valid for at least six months after your arrival date.

faqs.question: Is Tanzania safe to visit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tanzania is a peaceful and welcoming country and millions of tourists visit every year. As anywhere, use common sense in towns and keep valuables in your hotel safe. On tour, our team is with you all the time.

faqs.question: Do I need vaccinations?
faqs.answer: A yellow fever certificate is required if you arrive from, or transit through, a country with a risk of yellow fever. Speak to your doctor or a travel clinic about malaria tablets and routine vaccines before you travel.

faqs.question: How do I book with Nomad Explorer Tours?
faqs.answer: Send us an enquiry through the website or message us on WhatsApp with your dates and group size. We reply with a free itinerary and quote and adjust it until it suits you. Your trip is confirmed when we receive the deposit.

faqs.question: How do I pay?
faqs.answer: You can pay the deposit and balance by bank transfer or securely online by card through our payment link. Safari lodge packages need a 50% deposit and camping safaris a 30% deposit; the balance is due 65 days before arrival.

faqs.question: Can you tailor a trip for me?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Every private trip can be changed: add days, change hotels, combine a climb with a safari or Zanzibar, or start on any date that suits you. Just tell us what you have in mind.
